metaTitle: What Baby Cockroaches Look Like, by Species
metaDescription: Baby cockroaches (nymphs) are small, wingless copies of adults. German nymphs are dark, striped and 1/8 to 9/16 inch. See each species and look-alikes.
h1: What Do Baby Cockroaches Look Like? Nymphs by Species, Size and Color
dek: Cockroach nymphs differ by species in size, color and markings. Here is how to tell them from adults, bed bugs and beetles, and what finding them says about an infestation.
excerpt: What baby cockroaches look like: German, American, Oriental, brownbanded and smokybrown nymphs by size and color, why some look white, and what finding them means.

quickAnswer.lead: **Baby cockroaches, called nymphs, look like small, wingless versions of the adults, with a broad, flat body, long antennae and a color pattern that depends on the species.** German nymphs measure 1/8 to 9/16 inch and carry dark stripes; American and Oriental nymphs run from grayish or reddish brown to black. [Rutgers University's German cockroach fact sheet](https://njaes.rutgers.edu/fs1322/) gives the size range.
bullets: German nymphs are 1/8 to 9/16 inch (3 to 14 mm) long, dark, and marked with two dark stripes down the back.
American nymphs start grayish brown and turn reddish brown after the first few molts, while Oriental nymphs are reddish brown to black.
Young smokybrown nymphs are black with two white bands and white-tipped antennae, and brownbanded nymphs carry two broad brownish bands.
A cockroach that has just shed its skin is white and usually darkens within hours.
Nymphs make up about 80 percent of an actively growing German cockroach population, so they are the stage you are most likely to find.

body.text: What do baby cockroaches look like?

A baby cockroach, called a nymph, looks like a smaller, wingless copy of the adult, with the same broad, flat body and long antennae. [UC IPM](https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/cockroaches/), the University of California's pest management program, explains that cockroaches grow by gradual metamorphosis, so nymphs resemble adults and feed the same way but lack fully developed wings and cannot reproduce. There is no grub or cocoon stage: [Texas A&M AgriLife Extension](https://extensionentomology.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2016/07/E-359-Cockroach-biology-and-management-2012.pdf) describes a life cycle of just three stages, egg, nymph and adult.

What changes from one species to the next is color, markings and final size. A nymph in a kitchen cabinet may be dark with two stripes, while one near a floor drain may be reddish brown. [The complete cockroach reference for US homes](/learn/cockroaches) covers the adult species in depth, so this page concentrates on the young.

Three features mark almost any cockroach, nymphs included, whatever the color. Texas A&M describes a flattened body whose head is hidden from above by a plate-like shield called the pronotum, long and thin antennae, and elongated, spiny legs that let the insect run surprisingly fast. Most species are also nocturnal, hiding by day and feeding at night.

body.text: Color alone is a poor guide. Texas A&M notes that cockroaches range through brown, black, tan, reddish orange and pale green, and a nymph often differs in color from the adult of its own species, as the sections below show. Match the markings and the size first, then the shade.
How do you tell baby cockroaches apart by species?
Start with the markings, then check where you found the insect. The table pulls together what the extension sources linked on this page report for five common household species.

body.text: German cockroach nymphs

German nymphs turn up indoors: Texas A&M notes that German cockroaches spend their lives indoors. [Rutgers University](https://njaes.rutgers.edu/fs1322/) measures them at 1/8 to 9/16 inch (3 to 14 mm), and [the University of Florida's species profile](https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/IN128) describes them as dark brown to black with distinct dark bands along the shield behind the head. Texas A&M adds that the two dark stripes run down the whole thorax and abdomen and that nymphs show wing pads. Adults are 1/2 to 5/8 inch, so the biggest nymphs are nearly adult length; the missing wings, not the size, give them away. [The German cockroach guide](/blog/german-cockroaches) covers adults, spread and control.
American cockroach nymphs

American cockroach nymphs start out grayish brown and turn more reddish brown after the first few molts, according to Texas A&M, which notes that the species is also known as the waterbug or palmetto bug. The adult is the largest species on this page at 1 1/2 to 2 inches, and adults of both sexes can fly; nymphs cannot, because they have no fully developed wings. The sources reviewed give no length for American nymphs, so judge by proportion: a small, wingless, reddish-brown roach with long antennae. UC IPM puts the egg case at about 3/8 inch with about 12 young, far fewer than a German case. Because the name water bug gets attached to several different insects, [water bugs versus cockroaches](/blog/water-bugs-vs-cockroaches) sorts out which is which.
Oriental cockroach nymphs

Oriental cockroach nymphs are uniformly reddish brown to black, according to Texas A&M, so there are no stripes or bands to look for. The adult is dark brown to black and about 1 1/4 inches long, does not fly, and keeps short wings for life, so a short-winged adult can resemble a large nymph. Texas A&M puts development from egg to adult at an average of 575 to 600 days, and UC IPM puts the egg case at about 3/8 inch.
Brownbanded cockroach nymphs

Brownbanded nymphs carry bands instead of stripes. [Penn State Extension](https://extension.psu.edu/brown-banded-cockroaches) says both adults and nymphs show two broad brownish bands across the body, one at the base of the abdomen and one at mid-abdomen. Adults are about 1/2 inch long, close to a German cockroach, and UC IPM adds light bands on the wings and the sides of the pronotum.

Where the insect turns up helps. UC IPM lists crevices in electrical appliances, behind wall decorations and inside hollow furniture legs, and Penn State says brownbanded cockroaches favor warm, dry places nearer the ceiling than the floor and away from water, such as pantries, closets and dressers. A banded baby roach in a bedroom closet therefore points toward brownbanded rather than German. UC IPM adds that females glue egg cases of about 1/4 inch to ceilings, beneath furniture or in closets.
Smokybrown cockroach nymphs

Young smokybrown nymphs look nothing like their parents. Texas A&M describes them as black with two white bands on the body and white-tipped antennae, turning uniformly reddish brown as they age. UC IPM describes the nymphs in similar terms: dark brown, with white segments at the end of the antennae and across the back. Adults are 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 inches, dark brown to black, with wings that extend beyond the abdomen. The species lives mostly outdoors, especially in the humid South, so a banded black nymph indoors has probably come in from outside.

body.text: How can you tell a baby cockroach from a small adult?

Wings are the clearest difference. UC IPM says nymphs lack fully developed wings, while adult cockroaches have membranous wings. Texas A&M adds that German nymphs show wing pads, and that adult German cockroaches have wings reaching the end of the abdomen even though they do not fly.

items: **Wings.** A winged roach is an adult, even a small one. [Some adult species do fly](/blog/can-cockroaches-fly), but a nymph never does.
**Size.** German nymphs top out near 9/16 inch while adults run 1/2 to 5/8 inch, so size separates only the smaller nymphs.

**Exceptions.** Oriental adults keep short wings all their lives, and Penn State says female brownbanded adults are stouter than males, with wings that do not cover the abdomen. Both can pass for nymphs, so compare length with the adult sizes in the table above.
**Egg case.** Nymphs are not reproductively active, so a roach carrying an egg case is an adult female.

body.text: A tiny winged roach is therefore a small adult species, not a baby. German and brownbanded adults are both about half an inch, and Texas A&M warns that the Asian and field cockroaches look very similar to the German cockroach and may be found outdoors in some areas of Texas. UC IPM likewise says field cockroaches are often mistaken for German cockroaches.
Why do some baby cockroaches look white?

A white cockroach has just shed its skin. UC IPM says cockroaches are white immediately after molting and darken as the new outer covering hardens, usually within hours. A German nymph molts five to six times before adulthood according to Rutgers, and the University of Florida reports six as the number most often given, so it passes through that pale stage that many times.

That has two practical uses. A white roach is the same insect that will usually look brown or black again within hours, not a separate kind. And the skins it leaves behind count as evidence: UC IPM lists cast skins alongside droppings, egg cases and live or dead roaches as signs of cockroach activity. Rutgers adds that the shed skins of German cockroaches, like their feces and dead bodies, contain allergens that are asthma triggers.

body.text: How big are baby cockroaches, and how long do they take to grow up?

German nymphs measure 1/8 to 9/16 inch (3 to 14 mm) and need about 50 to 60 days to become adults, while the large species take more than a year and a half. The size range comes from Rutgers and is the only nymph measurement in the sources reviewed. For the other species the useful benchmark is adult length, which nymphs approach with each molt: about 1/2 inch for brownbanded, 1 1/4 inches for Oriental and 1 1/2 to 2 inches for American cockroaches.

body.text: The gap between species is the main point. Texas A&M's 50 to 60 days for a German nymph applies at average indoor temperatures, and it says warmer temperatures shorten development; Rutgers puts the whole German life cycle at about 100 days. Texas A&M gives American and smokybrown cockroaches an average of 600 days to reach adulthood, and Oriental cockroaches 575 to 600 days from egg to adult. A German colony can therefore complete a generation in about 100 days, while the large species need more than a year and a half.
Is it a baby cockroach, a bed bug nymph or a beetle?

Three checks sort most look-alikes: a shield-like plate that hides the head from above, stripes or bands on the back, and hard wing covers. The table sets a German nymph beside the two usual suspects.

body.text: Shape alone will not settle it. Cockroach nymphs and bed bug nymphs are both flat, and their size ranges overlap. UC IPM's bed bug description gives an oval, flat body and pale to rusty color but mentions no stripes or bands, so bold dark stripes or bands point to a cockroach nymph rather than a bed bug. [What bed bugs look like at each stage](/blog/what-do-bed-bugs-look-like) and [the insects most often mistaken for bed bugs](/blog/bugs-that-look-like-bed-bugs) cover the other side of the comparison.

The beetle test applies to adults: UC IPM notes that people confuse cockroaches with beetles, but adult cockroaches have membranous wings and lack the thick, hardened forewings of beetles. For the wider list of look-alikes, including crickets, ground beetles and wood roaches, [bugs that look like cockroaches](/blog/bugs-that-look-like-cockroaches) goes through each with a comparison table.

body.text: What does finding baby cockroaches tell you?

It tells you eggs have hatched somewhere close, which means adults are breeding nearby, though not always inside your walls. In an actively growing German cockroach population about 80 percent of the insects are nymphs, as Rutgers and the University of Florida both report, so in that case nymphs are the stage you should expect to meet. UC IPM says the same of cockroach populations generally: nymphs are typically the most abundant stage. After hatching, Texas A&M adds, nymphs tend to stay in dark, protected cracks that they often share with adults.
Where the nymph is matters as much as the fact that it exists:

items: **In the open during the day.** Texas A&M says that seeing cockroaches by day usually means a lot of them are around, noting that a German cockroach spends about 75 percent of its life in cracks 1/32 to 3/16 inch wide.
**A German nymph indoors.** German cockroaches spend their lives indoors, so a German nymph points to a colony somewhere in the building, usually in warm cracks near food and water.

**A large-species nymph indoors.** American, Oriental and smokybrown cockroaches live mostly outdoors but may move in. Texas A&M names poorly sealed doors, roof soffits and floor drains as entry routes for the larger types, so check those before assuming a colony inside.

body.text: Other signs help confirm what the nymphs suggest. Texas A&M says German cockroach droppings look like crushed pepper, and UC IPM lists dark spots or smears of fecal matter, cast skins and egg cases. No source reviewed sets a number of nymphs that counts as an infestation, which is why the sticky traps below are the way to find out how many there are. A separate guide traces [how cockroaches get into a home](/blog/where-do-cockroaches-come-from), whether carried in, through shared walls or up from drains.
What should you do after finding baby cockroaches?
Confirm the species, trap to find where they are, remove food, water and hiding places, and use bait in many small spots. In order:

items: **Identify one.** Catch a nymph in a jar or photograph it, and compare the stripes, bands and size with the species table above.

**Set sticky traps.** UC IPM recommends glue boards at the junctions of floors and walls and close to places where roaches are suspected, checked daily for several days to see where the most are caught. Texas A&M adds spots next to doors, behind laundry appliances and under stoves and refrigerators, and says traps suit monitoring better than control. A separate guide compares [how glue boards and bait stations do different jobs](/blog/best-roach-traps-canada).

**Look where they hide.** Texas A&M advises a good flashlight for spotting cockroaches and their signs, and says a household hair dryer blowing hot air into a hiding place can flush them out because they dislike heat and moving air.

**Remove food, water and cover.** Texas A&M advises cleaning floors and counters, fixing water leaks, reducing clutter, emptying pet bowls each night and sealing cracks and gaps around sinks and plumbing.

**Use bait in many small placements.** Texas A&M calls baits among the most effective insecticides for cockroaches in homes and says many small, pea-sized gel placements work better than a few large ones. If a bait has not controlled the population within 2 to 3 weeks, it suggests trying a different bait with a new active ingredient. Follow the product label for where and how much to apply.

**Skip bug bombs.** Texas A&M says total-release aerosols generally do not eliminate cockroaches because they do not reach the cracks where most hide, and that sprays are far less effective than baits against German cockroaches.
**Vacuum with a HEPA filter.** Texas A&M notes that vacuuming removes cockroaches and the crumbs they feed on, and that cockroach hiding places often contain allergens that can cause asthma.

body.title: The label is the law
body.text: Every bait, dust and spray is a pesticide. Use a product only where and how its label directs, and keep it away from children, pets and food surfaces.

If the nymphs are German, [the full control program for German cockroaches](/blog/german-cockroaches) goes further, and [a bait-first walkthrough for clearing cockroaches](/blog/how-to-get-rid-of-cockroaches-canada) lays out the steps in more detail. If bite-like marks are what led you to look, [what is documented about cockroach bites](/blog/do-cockroaches-bite) sets out the evidence. If traps keep filling after several weeks of correct baiting, or neighbors in your building have roaches too, a licensed pest professional can inspect the whole building.

faqs.question: Is there a nest if I find baby cockroaches?
faqs.answer: The sources reviewed describe hiding places, not nests. Texas A&M AgriLife Extension says that after hatching, nymphs tend to stay in dark, protected cracks and crevices that they often share with adult cockroaches. Finding nymphs therefore points to a hiding place nearby, usually behind or under appliances, inside cabinets or in wall gaps near food and water. Sticky traps set along walls and near those spots, then checked daily for several days, show where the most roaches are being caught.

faqs.question: Can baby cockroaches fly?
faqs.answer: No. UC IPM says nymphs do not have fully developed wings, so none of them can fly. Some adult cockroaches can fly. Texas A&M says adult American cockroaches of both sexes can, while adult German cockroaches have wings but do not fly. A small roach with full wings is therefore an adult of a small species, not a baby that has learned to fly.

faqs.question: Are baby cockroaches dangerous?
faqs.answer: The sources reviewed do not single out nymphs as more or less risky than adults. Texas A&M says cockroaches may transfer disease-causing organisms, that German cockroaches are associated with allergies and asthma, and that cockroach hiding places often contain allergens that can cause asthma. Rutgers adds that German cockroach feces, shed skins and dead bodies contain allergens that are asthma triggers, and growing nymphs leave shed skins behind. If anyone in the home has asthma or allergy symptoms that seem worse indoors, mention the infestation to a healthcare provider, and vacuum with a HEPA filter during cleanup.

faqs.question: How many baby cockroaches hatch from one egg case?
faqs.answer: It depends on the species. UC IPM gives about 30 young for a German cockroach egg case and about 12 for an American cockroach case, and Texas A&M gives 30 to 40 for the German species. Penn State Extension reports an average of 13 eggs per brownbanded cockroach capsule. Together with a German life cycle of about 100 days, against an average of about 600 days for an American cockroach to reach adulthood, that is why a German infestation can build faster than one made up of the larger species.

faqs.question: What is a tiny black cockroach with white stripes?
faqs.answer: A likely match in the southern states is a young smokybrown cockroach. Texas A&M describes the younger nymphs as black with two white bands on the body and white-tipped antennae, turning uniformly reddish brown as they get older. Adult smokybrown cockroaches are 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 inches long and live mostly outdoors, in places such as mulch, palm fronds and tree holes, so a banded black nymph indoors has likely wandered in from outside.
